title: How Iman Gadzhi finds SMMA prospects: networking, manual sourcing, software and freelancers
summary: Iman breaks down four ways to build a prospect list for an agency: networking, manual lead sourcing, lead software, and outsourcing to B2B lead gen freelancers. He explains the quantity vs quality trade-off of each and how to pick a combination based on your network, time and money.

principles.text: Use your network first; warm contacts and referrals are the easiest way to land your first client.
principles.quote: in my humble opinion it's the easiest way to sign your first client

principles.text: Be honest that you're a beginner; business owners respect it, and ask every contact for referrals.
principles.quote: people really appreciate honesty and most business owners have been in the same position as you and they respect it

principles.text: Manual lead sourcing (Google Maps, LinkedIn, Instagram, directories) gives the best lead quality and costs $0, but is slow.
principles.quote: the advantage of manual lead sourcing is the quality of the prospect because you are finding everything yourself

principles.text: Lead software trades some quality for huge volume and time savings; clean the list and use verification tools.
principles.quote: the quality of the list does suffer a bit but is the trade-off worth it in my opinion 100%

principles.text: Outsource list building to freelancers like you outsource delivery, but test with the cheapest tier first and check reviews.
principles.quote: always buy the first tier even if each Prospect costs a little bit more because this will allow you to use the list and judge the quality of it

principles.text: Choose your prospecting mix by network, time and money; prospecting is ongoing, so keep the list big.
principles.quote: prospecting is an ongoing task so build the habit of always keeping your prospecting list as big as possible
